name: BQ25886RGER
title: BQ25886: standalone 2-cell, 2 A boost-mode Li-ion charger with power path, BC1.2 detection and OTG buck output
summary: A charger for two-cell (2s) Li-ion and Li-polymer packs fed from a 5 V USB source: a 1.5 MHz synchronous boost converter lifts the 4.3 V to 6.2 V input up to the pack, with the input blocking FET, both switches, the battery FET and the bootstrap diode all inside a 4 mm × 4 mm VQFN-24. The converter feeds a system rail (SYS) held at no less than 6.2 V typ, and an 18 mΩ typ FET joins SYS to the pack, so the system runs at once with a flat or missing pack and the pack tops up the system when the input falls short. With no I2C port, charge voltage (8.2, 8.4, 8.7 or 8.8 V), charge current (up to 2.2 A) and the input current ceiling are set by resistors on VSET, ICHGSET and ILIM; D+/D- detection picks the source's current limit, and the OTG pin runs the converter backwards as a 5.1 V buck from the pack onto VBUS for up to 2 A.
key_figures: 4.3 V to 6.2 V operating; 20 V absolute maximum
30 mA to 2200 mA, set by RICHGSET (KICHGSET 3810 Ω/A)
500 mA to 3.3 A; ILIM pin IINMAX = 1110 A·Ω / RILIM
93.4 % at 5 V in, 7.6 V pack, 1 A charge

pins.name: D-
pins.function: USB data line, negative side. Used with D+ for BC1.2 source detection, data-contact detection and secondary detection included. Misprint: an NC entry also carries number 1; it should read D- only.

pins.name: STAT
pins.function: Charge status. Pulled up through 10 kΩ. Low while charging; high when charge is done or turned off; toggles at 1 Hz on any fault.

pins.name: /CE
pins.function: Charge enable, active low. Low lets the pack charge. A 900 kΩ internal resistor pulls it low.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: OTG
pins.function: On-The-Go enable. High turns on the buck output from the pack to VBUS; low turns it off.

pins.name: VSET
pins.function: Charge voltage select by a resistor to GND: under 18 kΩ (or shorted) gives 8.2 V; 39 kΩ ±10 % gives 8.8 V; 75 kΩ ±10 % gives 8.7 V; over 150 kΩ (or open) gives 8.4 V.

pins.name: TS
pins.function: Pack temperature input for an NTC thermistor. Two resistors, REGN to TS and TS to GND, set the temperature window; outside it, charging stops. 103AT-2 thermistor recommended.

pins.name: ILIM
pins.function: Input current ceiling. A resistor to ground sets IINMAX = KILIM / RILIM; the loop holds the pin at 0.8 V, and below that the pin voltage tracks input current, IIN = KILIM × VILIM / (RILIM × 0.8 V). Shorted to GND, the ILIM ceiling is at its maximum. Settings under 500 mA are not supported. Must not be left open.

pins.name: /PG
pins.function: Power good, active low. Pulled up through 10 kΩ. Low when the input is inside VVBUS_OP and can supply more than IPOORSRC.

pins.name: ICHGSET
pins.function: Charge current set by a resistor to GND, 30 mA (114 Ω) to 2.2 A (8 kΩ). Pre-charge and termination currents are one tenth of it, floored at 30 mA and 10 mA typ. Shorted to GND gives the 30 mA minimum; left open, charging is off.

pins.name: REGN
pins.function: Internal LDO output that biases the chip and the gate drivers. Bypass to GND with 4.7 µF ceramic. Current limit 50 mA.

pins.name: BTST
pins.function: High-side gate-drive supply; the internal bootstrap diode's cathode. A 47 nF capacitor goes from SW to BTST.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Battery connection. At least 10 µF, after derating, close between BAT and GND.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Battery connection; same node as pin 13.

pins.name: SYS
pins.function: System rail, the boost output. The internal battery FET sits between SYS and BAT; when the pack is below the minimum system voltage the converter holds SYS up. 2 × 22 µF, after derating, close between SYS and power ground.

pins.name: SYS
pins.function: System rail; same node as pin 15.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switching node; the switched end of the inductor.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switching node; same node as pin 17.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: PMID
pins.function: Drain side of the internal input blocking FET, the converter's input node. VBUS plus PMID need 10 µF or more of low-ESR capacitance after derating, at least 1 µF of it at VBUS and the rest at PMID; 10 µF is the usual PMID value.

pins.name: PMID
pins.function: Converter input node; same node as pin 21.

pins.name: VBUS
pins.function: Supply input from the external DC source. Bypass to GND with 1 µF or more of ceramic capacitance right at the chip.

pins.name: D+
pins.function: USB data line, positive side. Used with D- for BC1.2 source detection, data-contact detection and secondary detection included.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad. Soldered to board ground for heat and strength, with thermal vias under it to the ground plane; the single point where analog and power ground meet.

circuits.title: Standalone typical application, 2s pack, 5 V / 3 A USB input
circuits.description: A 5 V, 3 A USB source feeds VBUS with 1 µF at the pin; PMID carries 10 µF plus an optional 30 µF, and the 1 µH inductor runs from PMID to SW. 47 nF from SW to BTST supplies the high-side gate drive and 4.7 µF bypasses REGN. SYS feeds the system load with 44 µF and BAT goes to the 2s pack with 10 µF. RILIM 383 Ω, RVSET 150 kΩ and RICHGSET 5.7 kΩ to ground set the input ceiling, an 8.4 V charge voltage and the charge current. The pack's 10 kΩ NTC sits from TS to ground with 5.23 kΩ from REGN and 30.1 kΩ to ground setting the temperature window. STAT and /PG each sink an LED fed through 2.2 kΩ from VREF. A host drives OTG and /CE and shares the D+ and D- lines.

RILIM 383 Ω sets 2.9 A (1110 A·Ω / 383 Ω); the design table gives 2.4 A for the input current limit.

operation.text: Four FETs are inside: Q1 (QBLK) is the input blocking FET between VBUS and PMID, Q2 (QHS) and Q3 (QLS) are the high- and low-side switches of the boost stage, and Q4 (QBAT) links SYS to the pack. The bootstrap diode for the high-side driver is inside as well.
Internal bias comes from whichever of VBUS or BAT has passed its UVLO rising threshold, and once either has, the battery FET driver is live.
With only a pack above VBAT_UVLO_RISING, the battery FET turns on and SYS runs straight from the pack. REGN stays off to keep battery drain low.

On plug-in the chip qualifies the source, runs D+/D- detection to set the input current limit, starts REGN and then starts the converter. Qualification needs VBUS below the OVP threshold and above VPOORSRC while IPOORSRC (15 mA typ) is drawn. An over-voltage source is retried once it clears; a weak source is retried every 2 s, and after seven failures in a row the chip goes to HIZ, leaving the pack to run the system. A fresh plug-in is then needed to restart.

Detection runs data-contact detection, then primary, then secondary detection, per USB BC1.2, and also recognises non-standard dividers. SDP gives 500 mA, CDP 1.5 A, DCP 3.0 A, divider 3 1 A, divider 1 2.1 A, divider 4 2.4 A and an unknown 5 V adapter 500 mA. /PG goes low when detection completes. The input limit in use is the lower of the detection result (or the ICO result on a DCP) and the ILIM pin setting.

REGN biases the chip, drives the gates of QHS and QLS and can supply the TS divider and the STAT and /PG pull-ups. It comes on once VBUS is above UVLO in boost mode (or below it in buck mode), the source has qualified, detection has set the input limit and a 220 ms delay has passed. Otherwise the chip is in HIZ with REGN off, taking less than IVBUS_HIZ from VBUS.

With the input limit set, /PG goes low and switching starts. Before charging, IBAT_DISCHG is applied to check for a pack; the battery FET stays on to charge it and SYS ramps up with soft-start. The boost runs at a fixed 1.5 MHz. At light load, while the pack is below the minimum system voltage or charging is off, it moves to PFM, with duty cycle set by the SYS to VBUS ratio.

ICO finds the most current a source can deliver without pulling it into VINDPM. On this part it runs only when a DCP is detected. It keeps adjusting IINDPM and, once settled, holds that value until a new source is plugged in, VINDPM is entered or VBUS OVP occurs. The ILIM pin limit still caps the result.

The converter can run in reverse as a buck from the pack onto VBUS, meeting the 500 mA USB OTG requirement and delivering up to 2.0 A. It starts when BAT is above VOTG_BAT, VBUS is below VVBUS_PRESENT, OTG is high, TS is between the BHOT and BCOLD thresholds, and 30 ms have passed since enable.

The battery FET separates SYS from the pack. With a deeply discharged pack SYS is still held above the fixed 6.2 V typ minimum: the FET runs linearly and SYS sits about 200 mV above the minimum. Once the pack is above the minimum the FET is fully on and SYS is the pack voltage plus the FET drop. With charging off (pack above the minimum) or terminated, SYS is held about 50 mV above the pack.

The chip watches input current and voltage. When system load plus charge current would exceed the input current limit, or would pull VBUS down to VINDPM (4.3 V typ), charge current is cut until the input sits at its limit. On a DCP, entering VINDPM makes ICO lower the limit. If charge current reaches zero and the source is still overloaded, SYS falls below the pack and supplement mode begins.

When SYS drops below the pack, the battery FET turns on and the pack shares the load with the input. As discharge current grows the FET gate is driven harder until it is fully on, after which the FET drop rises in proportion to current. The FET turns off again when the pack falls below VBAT_UVLO_RISING.

With /CE low the chip charges on its own: voltage from VSET, current from ICHGSET, pre-charge and termination at one tenth of ICHG, JEITA temperature profile, 12 h safety timer. A cycle starts when the converter is running with no TS fault and no timer fault. It ends when current is under the termination level, the pack is above the recharge threshold and the chip is not in DPM or thermal regulation. A pack that sags 200 mV below VREG starts a new cycle; toggling /CE after a finished charge also starts one.

Five phases: trickle charge below VBAT_SHORT, pre-charge below VBAT_LOWV, constant current, constant voltage, then a top-off timer. In DPM or thermal regulation the actual current is below the setting, termination is held off and the safety timer counts at half speed.

At termination the battery FET turns off and STAT goes high; the converter keeps powering SYS, and the battery FET can turn on again for supplement mode. Termination is held off in input current, input voltage or thermal regulation. The termination threshold is ICHG / 10.

Charging starts only with TS between the VT1 and VT5 thresholds and stops outside them until the pack returns to range. Between T1 and T2 (0 °C to 10 °C) charge current drops to 20 % of ICHG; between T3 and T5 (45 °C to 60 °C) charge voltage drops to 8.0 V. In either band termination is off. The TS divider of RT1 from REGN and RT2 to ground around a 103AT NTC sets the thresholds.

The fast-charge timer counts at half speed during input voltage, input current or thermal regulation, so a 12 h timer that spends the whole cycle in input current regulation runs out at 24 h. It pauses during charge-disabling faults and supplement mode and resumes afterwards. It resets when a cycle stops and restarts (/CE toggled, or a full pack falls below recharge) and when the pack crosses between pre-charge and fast charge. A fixed 2 h pre-charge timer, running while VBAT < VBAT_LOWV, follows the same rules.
/PG goes low when VBUS is above UVLO rising, below the OVP threshold, holds above VPOORSRC (3.7 V typ) under IPOORSRC load, and detection has finished.

Open-drain status that can drive an LED: low while charging, high when charge is complete or disabled, blinking at 1 Hz on a charge fault or an OTG suspend for a TS fault. With no pack fitted it blinks as the BAT capacitance charges and discharges.

The ILIM resistor sets a hardware input current ceiling; the chip regulates ILIM at 0.8 V and enters input current regulation above it. Below 0.8 V the pin voltage is proportional to input current. Left open, ILIM floats above 0.8 V and input current is held at zero.

VBUS above VVBUS_OV stops switching at once, restarting when it clears. VBUS below VPOORSRC during operation also stops switching, with an automatic retry. SYS over-voltage, 350 mV above the system regulation target, stops the converter at once to clamp load-transient overshoot. If VSYS comes within 250 mV of VBUS a system short is flagged and switching stops, with automatic recovery.

In buck mode the chip monitors VBUS and the currents in QBLK and QLS. VBUS above VOTG_OVP stops switching and leaves buck mode. Output current is held by a constant-current loop; on a VBUS short the output shuts off and retries seven times, then OTG is disabled.

In boost mode the chip trims charge current to hold the junction at 120 °C; termination is then off and the safety timer runs at half speed. Above TSHUT the converter stops, restarting once the die cools below the falling threshold. Thermal shutdown also protects buck mode.
While charging, if the pack rises 4 % above the regulation voltage, charging stops at once.
SYS can be supplied from a 3.9 V to 6.2 V source rated 500 mA or more on VBUS, or from a 2s pack above VBAT_UVLO on BAT. For full output power to SYS the source needs at least 3 A.
1.5 MHz switching allows small inductors and capacitors. Saturation current must exceed input current plus half the ripple; ripple peaks near 50 % duty.

Low-ESR X5R or X7R ceramics close to PMID and GND, rated well above the input voltage; 25 V or more for a 5 V input. At least 10 µF for up to 3.3 A of input current, 44 µF on PMID for best performance, and at least 1 µF at VBUS. A long, high-impedance cable drops a lot of voltage under inrush.
Low-ESR X5R or X7R ceramics close to SYS and GND, 16 V rating or more, at least 44 µF for up to 2.2 A of boost output current.

When the input must never exceed a limit, size RILIM for the low end of the regulation spread: for a 900 mA ceiling with about ±8.9 % accuracy at that setting, design for 819.9 mA, and allow for resistor tolerance too.

In order of priority: SYS capacitor tight to SYS and GND; PMID capacitor tight to PMID and power ground; SW trace to the inductor short, with little copper area but wide enough for input current and little capacitance to other nets; decoupling capacitors next to the chip on the same side. Run analog ground apart from power ground and join them only at the thermal pad (or through a 0 Ω resistor). Solder the exposed pad to ground with enough thermal vias under the chip, and size vias for the current they carry.
